propositions: 827 truncated bridge-echo comments lacking the reconciler marker were removed from three Jira issues (REB-2605, REB-1931, REB-1567) using a two-condition identification rule: presence of truncation suffix AND absence of marker.
The marker is missing from these comments because truncation appends the marker after the body, so the 32767-character cut removes it; this is the defect documented separately in ticket 5931.

Keep-one rule preserves the oldest copy (lowest comment id) of each distinct normalized body; no comment was id-referenced at execution time, so this rule is safe but must invert for the post-re-enable final sweep.
The first bridge pass after re-enabling will re-post one copy per distinct truncated comment (roughly 8 across three issues) before deduplication resumes; this expected re-post is not a regression.
Backup completeness is proven by exact reconciliation: backup count minus deleted count equals observed count after deletion on all three issues independently.
Phase 2 deletions must precede bridge re-enablement; the final cleanup sweep must invert the keep-rule to preserve the newly-posted copy whose id is recorded in comment_ids.
